item.text:
Research continuation completed across all selected chapters 1B–8B. I did not score the ruler.

Filesystem persistence remains blocked: the repository shell failed to initialize, so `research-ledger-manifest.json` could not be updated. The following provisional IDs are therefore a handoff patch, not persisted ledger changes.

### New evidence units

- `CONT-2026-IRN-1B-001` — IAEA safeguards reporting in 2023 continued to identify unresolved uranium traces at undeclared locations and insufficient Iranian cooperation. Target-year, system-attributable; Iran’s peaceful-use claims are contrary evidence. Links: `1B.3`, `1B.4`, `1B.7`, `1B.10`. [IAEA safeguards reporting](https://www.iranwatch.org/library/multilateral-organizations/international-atomic-energy-agency/iaea-report/npt-safeguards-agreement-islamic-republic-iran-gov20239)

- `CONT-2026-IRN-1B-002` — By September 2023, reporting based on IAEA findings described continued stockpile growth, no resolution of undeclared-site questions, and no restoration of monitoring equipment. Links: `1B.1`, `1B.3`, `1B.4`, `1B.10`. [Reuters/Iran Watch summary](https://www.iranwatch.org/news-brief/iran-expands-stock-near-weapons-grade-uranium-iaea-reports-no-progress)

- `CONT-2026-IRN-1B-003` — Conflict Armament Research documented Iranian-origin drone components and later identified Russian-produced variants derived from Iranian designs. This strengthens the transfer nexus but does not prove Khamenei personally ordered a 2023 transfer. Links: `1B.5`, `1B.6`, `1B.9`. [CAR field dispatches](https://www.conflictarm.com/field-dispatches/), [Washington Institute summary](https://www.washingtoninstitute.org/policy-analysis/irans-military-drone-program-security-implications-and-policy-responses)

- `CONT-2026-IRN-2B-001` — The technical drone record supports Iranian-origin technology in weapons used in Ukraine, while the exact timing, transaction, and ruler-level authorization remain unresolved. Links: `2B.2`, `2B.5`, `2B.6`, `2B.8`, `2B.9`.

- `CONT-2026-IRN-2B-002` — The March IAEA-Iran cooperation mechanism did not produce durable closure: later monitoring still reported unresolved safeguards questions and degraded verification. Links: `2B.1`, `2B.4`, `2B.7`, `2B.9`, `2B.10`. [IAEA-Iran joint statement](https://www.iaea.org/fr/newscenter/pressreleases/declaration-commune-de-lorganisation-iranienne-de-lenergie-atomique-oiea-et-de-lagence-internationale-de-lenergie-atomique-aiea)

- `CONT-2026-IRN-2B-003` — The December 2023 UN record indicates that the year ended with stockpiles far above JCPOA limits and diplomacy stalled. Links: `2B.1`, `2B.7`, `2B.10`. [UN Security Council coverage](https://press.un.org/en/2023/sc15536.doc.htm)

- `CONT-2026-IRN-3B-001` — Iran Human Rights’ 2023 annual report provides an additional execution-count source, while its NGO status requires corroboration and should not be treated as a complete national census. Links: `3B.1`, `3B.6`, `3B.7`, `3B.10`. [Iran Human Rights annual report](https://www.iranhr.net/media/files/Iran_Human_Rights-Annual_Report_2023.pdf)

- `CONT-2026-IRN-3B-002` — The UN mission’s lack of access and missing official arrest data remain the central observability limitation; this is not itself adverse evidence. Links: `3B.4`, `3B.8`, `3B.9`, `3B.10`. [UN Fact-Finding Mission update](https://www.unognewsroom.org/story/en/1688/hrc-53-fact-finding-mission-on-iran-05-july-2023/5273)

- `CONT-2026-IRN-4B-001` — The 2023 parliamentary-election preparation record shows unusually high candidate registration, but all candidates still required Guardian Council approval. This is contrary evidence to a total absence of participation, not evidence of open competition. Links: `4B.1`, `4B.2`, `4B.4`, `4B.8`. [Associated Press report](https://apnews.com/article/a740c368587fcddf4762eca14a29157c)

- `CONT-2026-IRN-4B-002` — The later election record confirms the continuing centrality of Guardian Council vetting and low participation, but because the vote occurred in 2024 it is usable only as continuity evidence, not a direct 2023 outcome. Links: `4B.1`, `4B.2`, `4B.8`, `4B.10`. [UK Parliament research briefing](https://commonslibrary.parliament.uk/irans-2024-elections/)

- `CONT-2026-IRN-5B-001` — World Bank poverty material identifies elevated inflation, living-cost pressure, and deterioration in household welfare; the causal contribution of sanctions and domestic policy remains mixed. Links: `5B.3`, `5B.8`, `5B.9`, `5B.10`. [World Bank Poverty and Equity Brief](https://databankfiles.worldbank.org/public/ddpext_download/poverty/987B9C90-CB9F-4D93-AE8C-750588BF00QA/current/Global_POVEQ_IRN.pdf)

- `CONT-2026-IRN-5B-002` — The World Bank’s 2024 outlook confirms oil-driven growth and employment recovery alongside elevated inflation, supporting a mixed—not collapse-only—economic record. Links: `5B.1`, `5B.3`, `5B.8`, `5B.9`, `5B.10`. [Macro Poverty Outlook](https://documents.worldbank.org/en/publication/documents-reports/documentdetail/099830404052427908)

- `CONT-2026-IRN-6B-001` — UNICEF’s 2023–2027 country programme documents formal state-linked priorities in child health, nutrition, education, water, sanitation, protection, and social protection. This establishes programme intent, not successful delivery. Links: `6B.1`, `6B.2`, `6B.3`, `6B.4`, `6B.9`. [UNICEF Iran country programme](https://www.unicef.org/iran/en/reports/unicef-and-islamic-republic-iran-country-programme-cooperation-2023-2027)

- `CONT-2026-IRN-6B-002` — WHO reporting frames access, financial hardship, medicines, vaccines, and health governance as active programme objectives; it does not establish nationwide 2023 outcome improvement. Links: `6B.2`, `6B.4`, `6B.5`, `6B.6`, `6B.10`. [WHO Iran country profile](https://www.who.int/about/accountability/results/who-results-report-2022-2023/country-profile/2023/iran-%28islamic-republic-of%29)

- `CONT-2026-IRN-7B-001` — Treasury’s patronage-network allegations remain institutionally important but are not adjudicated proof of Khamenei’s personal enrichment. No independent audit or domestic judicial finding was recovered. Links: `7B.3`, `7B.4`, `7B.5`, `7B.6`, `7B.9`.

- `CONT-2026-IRN-7B-002` — The absence of public asset declarations, domestic audits, or court findings remains an evidence gap rather than a negative integrity fact. Links: `7B.3`, `7B.4`, `7B.6`.

- `CONT-2026-IRN-8B-001` — The evidence supports strong implementation capacity for coercive control and selective diplomacy, but not broad welfare or institutional effectiveness. Links: `8B.2`, `8B.3`, `8B.5`, `8B.6`, `8B.7`, `8B.9`.

- `CONT-2026-IRN-8B-002` — UNICEF and WHO programme records provide positive evidence of formal service-planning machinery, but no independent evidence was recovered showing durable, population-wide implementation success in 2023. Links: `8B.2`, `8B.4`, `8B.6`, `8B.8`, `8B.10`.

### Honest shortfall

All chapters were attempted. The strongest recoveries were:

- `1B–2B`: improved IAEA chronology and technically grounded UAV-origin evidence.
- `3B–4B`: additional execution, election-preparation, and institutional-continuity material.
- `5B–6B`: stronger household-welfare and formal social-programme evidence.
- `7B`: no court-grade personal-integrity nexus recovered.
- `8B`: stronger distinction between coercive state capacity, formal programme machinery, and actual positive effectiveness.

Remaining gaps are genuine: direct Khamenei orders for most 2023 actions, independent personal financial records, representative service-outcome data, and a fully adjudicated UAV-transfer chain.
